criteria: Name the three core features of ADHD and explain how they differ from ordinary distraction.
Describe attention-related and hyperactive or impulsive signs across settings like home, school, and work.
Identify supports that can help, from behavior strategies to school accommodations.
Distinguish useful short-term anxiety from anxiety that overwhelms daily life.
Describe generalized anxiety, panic, and phobias in plain language.
Name common symptoms, risk factors, and the kinds of support that can help.
Describe immediate and long-term benefits of regular physical activity for brain and body.
State the general weekly activity guideline and adapt it to their own schedule.
Explain how movement relates to mood, sleep, and long-term health risks.
Describe common reactions after a traumatic event and how most ease over time.
Recognize signs that someone may need more support, including how children and teens can differ from adults.
List healthy coping steps and know when to contact crisis support.
Explain how depression differs from ordinary sadness.
Recognize common symptoms and describe how they can vary by age.
Describe what can help and when to reach out for support.
Describe rehearsal, chunking, elaborative rehearsal, and mnemonic devices.
Apply at least two evidence-based study strategies to real material.
Explain why distributed practice works better than cramming.
List signs that mental energy is running low.
Choose practical steps that may help them feel better.
Identify when to reach out to a provider or crisis support.
Define mental health as emotional, psychological, and social well-being.
Name several everyday practices that support mental health.
Describe one calming practice and recognize when to seek help.
Define emotion and distinguish it from mood.
Compare the major theories of emotion, from James-Lange to cognitive-mediational.
Name key limbic system structures involved in emotional processing.
Define operant conditioning and the law of effect.
Distinguish the four combinations of reinforcement and punishment.
Explain shaping and why variable ratio schedules are the most resistant to extinction.
Define personality as long-standing patterns of thinking, feeling, and behaving.
Trace how personality theories developed from the four temperaments to modern approaches.
Explain why phrenology was discredited as pseudoscience.
Name several small, repeatable self-care practices.
Match self-care areas such as sleep, movement, and connection to their own routine.
Recognize symptoms that call for more support from a provider.
Describe what sleep does for the brain and body.
State how much sleep their age group needs and what short sleep costs.
Apply several habits that improve sleep quality.
Define social connection in terms of the number, quality, and variety of relationships.
Explain how supportive relationships relate to health outcomes.
Distinguish emotional support from physical support and name a community source of each.
Describe consciousness as a continuum from full alertness to deep sleep.
Explain how the suprachiasmatic nucleus and melatonin regulate circadian rhythm.
Identify causes and costs of circadian disruption and sleep debt.
Define stress and recognize how it shows up in feelings, body, and behavior.
Name several practices that care for the mind under stress.
Name several practices that care for the body under stress.
Distinguish problem-focused from emotion-focused coping and describe when each fits.
Explain how perceived control and learned helplessness shape responses to stress.
Describe how social support buffers stress and name one stress-reduction technique.
Define cognition and describe what cognitive psychology studies.
Distinguish natural from artificial concepts and give an example of a prototype.
Explain how schemata speed up thinking and where they can mislead.
